Here are the quantitative parameters and values extracted from the text:

1. T_RM remain resident within the tissues for long periods of time: >1 year in mice.
2. Adoptively transferred CCR7−/− T_RM controlled Th1-mediated inflammation more efficiently than WT T_RM.
3. Large numbers of T_RM reportedly exit the skin during a cutaneous immune response in mice.
4. Graft survival was shorter for egress-incompetent T_reg compared to WT T_reg.
5. In a mouse model of delayed-type hypersensitivity, transgenic CD4+ Th1 cells displayed reduced migration from inflamed skin to the dLN relative to polyclonal CD4+ Th1 cells.
6. A significantly reduced number of antigen-specific cytotoxic CD8+ T cells (Tc1) migrated from the lung to the dLN in influenza-infected animals compared to antigen-unspecific Tc1 cells.
